title: Experiment evolution timeline and criterion matrix for rollout gating
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a single, reproducible experiment trajectory and a decision criterion matrix to standardize canary/A-B rollouts across Redwood services. The goal is to reduce manual judgement during traffic ramps and ensure consistent quality/cost trade-offs are enforced by automated gates.

Scope:
- Define four phased milestones (smoke, limited, ramp, steady) with explicit timeboxes and traffic ramps.
- Surface metric buckets (quality, latency, infrastructure, cost, user signal) and map primary/secondary metrics to each phase.
- Specify hard and soft thresholds, statistical confidence targets, and escalation paths.
- Produce runbook snippets for on-call, SRE and PM owners for each phase (who to page, who approves ramp steps).
- Integrate gating definitions with Console rollout UI and experiment orchestration hooks (API + webhook).

Unique contributions in this ticket (what makes this different):
- A criterion matrix (human-readable) that groups metrics into action buckets rather than single-metric gates (e.g., degrade quality vs. degrade infra vs. cost deviation).
- Automated hold decisions based on combined metric patterns (for example: small latency increase + token-cost decrease => allow; small latency increase + error spike => hold).
- Explicit short-circuit rollback conditions and a lightweight confidence calculator that factors sample size, effect size, and seasonality.

Success metrics:
- 80% of internal experiments use the matrix for ramp decisions within 2 cycles after release.
- Reduction in manual rollbacks triggered by delayed detection by 30% vs baseline.
- Time-to-safe-traffic (time between 0->100% or reserved capacity commit) reduced by 25% for routine model updates.

High-level timeline:
- Week 1 (smoke & spec): finalize metric buckets, owners, and runbook templates.
- Week 2 (pilot): wire into two active experiments (one Hosted API change, one Dedicated routing tweak).
- Week 3 (observe & iterate): collect pilot telemetry, tune thresholds.
- Week 4 (platform hooks): add Console gating UI annotations and webhook actions for hold/continue.

Criterion matrix (human-readable excerpt):
- Quality bucket: primary = regression rate on eval prompts (delta > 2% absolute), secondary = NPS/retention signals; action = hold & triage. Confidence target = 95% or bootstrap with >1k relevant requests.
- Latency bucket: primary = p95 token latency (delta > 20%), secondary = tail error rate; action = slow-roll or reduce traffic; if p95 delta >50% => hold.
- Infrastructure bucket: GPU OOMs, oom-rate >0.5% OR spikes in host_cpu >85% -> immediate hold + page SRE.
- Cost bucket: per-token cost delta >15% without quality improvement => pause to evaluate quantization/config.
- Combined rules: two soft signals from different buckets (e.g., latency + cost) escalate to PM review; any hard signal in infra or quality => immediate rollback.

Operational notes:
- Owners: PM (assignee) approves business-fraction ramp steps; SRE approves infra safety checks; Experiment owner (engineer) owns instrumentation and remediation steps.
- Data sources: Console metrics, feature-flag traffic logs, evaluation harness (Confluence eval suite), and dedicated dashboards in Grafana.

Artifacts and integrations referenced below.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Published matrix and runbook templates in Confluence; 2) Two pilot experiments wired to gates and webhook actions; 3) Dashboard panels showing gate health and decision events; 4) Post-pilot retrospective with threshold adjustments and a validated rollback playbook.
